latin_provenance.provenance_evidence: Wilson supplies a complete two-part prayer asking that the repeatedly received holy gifts be handled with sincere devotion and received with a faithful mind. PiusSecret keeps both linked predicates, their order, request frame and ending, but adds an offering preface, recasts the sacramental object, inserts Pius' intercession, omits semper, and reassigns the whole from postcommunion to Secret. The selected modern whole is not a one-name or one-functional-word substitution. Its new opening, object phrase, intercessory insertion, omission and change of liturgical role may form an expressive adaptation. Wilson proves the central petition is old, but does not establish the complete modern arrangement or its freedom from protection. No blanket sibling decision reaches it.

latin_provenance.publication_evidence: Qualified nonoriginal-adaptation assessment for this exact complete expression at moderate confidence. The complete Wilson1915 Ad complendum supplies the entire distinctive paired petition: request to treat the holy sacramental object with sincere devotion and receive it with faithful mind, in that order. In this exact target, a conventional acceptance-of-offerings ablative preface qualifies the same divine grant; divine mysteries is an ordinary sacramental designation, and the saint/title/intercession insertion is conventional functional wording. Omission of always and the repeatedly-filled relative clause abbreviates the old temporality without adding a new literary relationship. Considered jointly, the alterations adapt the intact distinctive paired petition to a Secret and factual saint intercession. The brief acceptance condition and sacramental/intercessory wording do not create a separately expressive new narrative, image or extended arrangement. On that bounded whole-expression finding, I accept this exact Latin and its independently faithful fresh English under publication-policy1 priority6. Strongest contrary and disposition: The offering preface and intercession are real additions; this is neither a single name substitution nor an exact old whole, and functional role change does not itself prove nonoriginality. A low originality threshold can protect a creative new arrangement even from old words. Here the actual new arrangement is ordinary dependent offering-acceptance and intercession attached to one retained complete paired petition, rather than an independently individualized narrative or newly joined substantive petitions. The affirmative is limited to this exact expression at moderate confidence; no general saint/Secret adaptation permission follows. translations.text: Graciously receive our offerings, we beseech Thee, O Lord, and grant that, through the intercession of Saint Pius, Supreme Pontiff, we may celebrate these divine mysteries with sincere devotion and receive them with a faithful mind. Through our Lord.
